name: cash and its fee paid in another currency both convert at the rate the record states
spec: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md, the ledger: a fill's value is its cash less its fee
working: 10 U (USD) bought for 1,260 CAD with a 10 CAD fee at 1.25 CAD per USD: cash 1,008 USD, fee 8 USD, value 1,000 USD
10 U sold for 1,490 CAD with a 10 CAD fee at 1.25: cash 1,192 USD, fee 8 USD, value 1,200 USD

name: a fee in a currency that is neither the instrument's nor the cash's, at no stated rate, leaves the fill's value unstated
spec: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md, the ledger: nothing the record does not state is worked out
working: 10 U (USD) bought for 1,000 USD with a 5 CAD fee and no rate: the lot opens with its quantity, its value waiting
10 U sold for 1,200 USD: the round trip closes, its P&L waiting on the fee's currency

name: a fill that states neither its cash nor its price has no value on the record
spec: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md, the ledger: a fill's value is its cash, or its price where no cash is stated
working: 100 X bought with no cash and no price: the lot opens with its quantity, its value waiting (never zero)
100 X sold for 1,200: the round trip's P&L waits on the purchase's value

name: price and cash are compared at the cash's cents: a difference each way is listed, one the cash's or the stated rate's rounding explains is not
spec: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md, the ledger: where a record states both and they disagree, the cash stands and the record is a problem
working: t1: 3 X at 33.333 is 99.999, 100.00 at the cash's cents, and the cash is 100.00: they agree
t2: 1 X at 10 against cash 10.50: the cash is more than the price says
t3: 2 X at 31 is 62 against cash 60: the price says more than the cash
t4: 2 X at 29 is 58.00 USD against 75 CAD at 1.25 CAD per USD, 60.00 USD: every cash and rate that round to 75 and 1.25 give 59.76 to 60.25, so the price disagrees

name: what a fill opens after closing part of it is exactly what the close left of its value
spec: docs/plans/stage-2-engine.md, the ledger: the parts of a fill add up to it exactly
working: 1 C bought for 100; 2 C sold for 199.999999999999: one closes the long, one opens a short
the close takes half, 99.9999999999995, which rounds half-even to 100.000000000000 at 12 places
the short opens with what is left, 99.999999999999, not a second half rounded the same way
the short is covered for 50: its P&L is 49.999999999999, and the two trips add to the cash, 49.999999999999
